series: 20-mile drive Short follow-up 1 of 3 (drive time on a small job)
hook: Charging $150 for a 2.5-hour clean? You lose $33.79
hook_say: Here is what a $150 price on a 2.5-hour job really pays once the drive is counted.

rows.label: Hours on site, 1 person
rows.why: The calculator's first example: a standard clean of a 2-bedroom home, 2.5 hours on site, one person, $8 of supplies.

rows.label: Round-trip miles
rows.why: A 15-mile round trip at 30 mph is 30 minutes behind the wheel.

rows.label: Your price now
rows.why: Type the price you charge today: $150.

rows.label: Drive time at your break-even rate
rows.why: Your break-even rate is $54.80 per paid hour, from $52,000 of take-home pay, $545 a month of costs and the taxes, spread over paid hours only. Half an hour of driving costs $27.40.

rows.label: Vehicle cost, 76 cents a mile
rows.why: 15 miles at the IRS rate of 76 cents a mile is $11.40.

rows.label: Price floor, zero profit
rows.why: Labor on site, drive time, mileage and supplies: $183.79 just to break even.

rows.label: At $150 you make
rows.why: At $150 the job pays $33.79 less than it costs you. The check line says it in plain words: below your floor.

fix.label: Quote, rounded up to the next $5
fix.why: With a 15% profit margin, rounded up to the next $5, the quote is $220. The Price Sheet does this for every job type at once.

note: Example numbers from the calculator. Yours go in the yellow cells.
